summary: A worked example of using IBM TSO at UCLA CCN over the network. It walks through logging on, creating a Fortran source with the editor, and running a batch compilation and foreground execution, with annotations explaining each step.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 390 shows a user working through TSO to write, compile and run a Fortran program. The program reads a number and prints its square root.

subtitle: A worked example of editing, compiling and running a Fortran program

tldr.problem: Users needed an example of compiling a program in batch and then running it interactively through TSO.
tldr.mechanism: The scenario logs into TSO, creates and saves a Fortran source file, submits it for compilation, checks its status and calls the resulting program.
tldr.outcome: The example demonstrates a complete workflow with a program that repeatedly reads a number and prints its square root.

today: RFC 390 is a worked TSO scenario dated September 1972. It demonstrates the commands and system responses shown in the document.

sections.title: Logging In and Creating Source Code
sections.content:
The scenario begins with a TSO logon using a user ID and password. The user opens EDIT, creates a new Fortran source data set and enters a program that prompts for a value, calculates its square root and prints the result.

The example shows commands for reviewing and changing a source line, listing the file and saving it before leaving the editor.
sections.plainLanguage: The user logs in, opens the editor and types a Fortran program. The example also shows how to inspect, change and save the source.

sections.title: Submitting the Program for Compilation
sections.content:
After allocating a library data set, the user submits the source file as a batch job. TSO assigns the job a name, and the user checks its progress with STATUS. When it finishes, the user examines the output listing and finds a step return code of 0.

The example then sends the output listing to the print queue.
sections.plainLanguage: The source is sent to a batch job for compilation. The user checks the job status and then looks at the output to see the compiler's return code.

sections.title: Running the Compiled Program
sections.content: The user allocates terminal input and output for the Fortran program and calls the load module. The program asks for values, including 3.141 and 4096, and prints the corresponding square roots shown in the example. The scenario ends with the user leaving TSO.
sections.plainLanguage: After compilation, the user runs the program at the terminal and enters values. The program prints the results before the user logs off.
